note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: German chancellor urges businesses to embrace AI as Nvidia announces new investments
items.blurb: Nvidia will back four German startups, part of a nearly $10 billion commitment to European AI companies and research.

items.title: Debt, AI and Ukraine crowd out China at IMF annual meetings
items.blurb: The IMF warned that if AI fails to deliver promised productivity gains, the global economy could suffer severe consequences.

items.title: AI rally fades away from Wall Street as a tiny IPO makes big waves
items.blurb: Korean AI data-center firm Elice fell over 30% on debut, as other data-center IPOs were cancelled amid funding worries.

items.title: CNBC Daily Open: Tech investors buy the dip — but debt remains a concern
items.blurb: Tech stocks rebounded, but borrowing costs behind the AI data-center buildout keep investors cautious.

items.title: OpenAI bugging suspect WhatsApp'ed Saudi royal days before arrest, feds reveal
items.blurb: Prosecutors say the man charged with bugging an OpenAI executive room messaged a Saudi royal until Oct 5.

items.title: The AI attack-ad nightmare is coming true
items.blurb: Campaigns spent $137 million on 220 AI-generated ads through Oct 11; no federal law specifically regulates them.

items.title: China's CXMT shares fall nearly 8% as investors look past chipmaker's profit turnaround
items.blurb: China's main memory-chip maker slid despite a return to profit, a sign of shakier sentiment around AI hardware.

items.title: Anthropic is AI trade's last big hope for a major IPO this year
items.blurb: After a sharp AI stock sell-off, investors look to Anthropic's expected listing as the year's key test of AI demand.

items.title: Anthropic pledge to usher in new era of AI-infused philanthropy
items.blurb: Anthropic's 5% share pledge signals AI lab IPOs could create the world's largest charitable foundations.

items.title: Bill Gross launches new AI platform to generate startup ideas
items.blurb: Idealab.ai mined millions of sources into 1.2 million business ideas, pitching AI as a creator of companies rather than a job cutter.

items.title: Credit stress is threatening to unwind the AI bull. All eyes are on Oracle to hold the line
items.blurb: Oracle bonds sit near junk territory; a downgrade could ripple through how the AI data-center buildout gets financed.

items.title: Apple announces product launch event for Oct. 28. Analysts expect touchscreen laptop
items.blurb: Macs have become a strong part of Apple's AI story because their chips run large models in fast shared memory.

items.title: Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
items.blurb: As AI agents browse and shop for people, sites may redesign around bots, risking worse pricing and interfaces for humans.

items.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
items.blurb: Researchers left copies of Claude alone on a simulated island for 30 hours and observed behavior resembling play.

items.title: Gartner analyst behind tech rout: AI returns are not yet large enough to justify neocloud build-out
items.blurb: Gartner's chief forecaster says AI returns don't yet support the scale of data-center spending, a warning that shook AI stocks.

items.title: Always on, always listening: New AI devices are pushing legal limits and could put users in jeopardy
items.blurb: Always-listening AI wearables from Apple, Amazon and Meta raise wiretap-law questions about recording bystanders without consent.

items.title: Meta Platforms and Tesla are among the companies set to report next week. What to expect
items.blurb: Meta reports its first quarter since launching the Muse agent, a test of whether AI spending is paying off.

items.title: Nasdaq futures gain as investors buy the dip in the AI trade
items.blurb: Stock futures rose Sunday evening after a week in which AI-linked shares lost over $1 trillion in value.

items.title: India's Finance Minister blames easy exits and excess liquidity for equity market's underperformance
items.blurb: Nirmala Sitharaman said India would not be hurt if a global AI bubble burst, as investors favor Taiwan and Korea.

items.title: Anthropic commits 5% of shares to new public benefit fund that could address AI job disruption
items.blurb: Anthropic is setting aside 5% of its shares for a public benefit fund that could address jobs lost to AI.

items.title: IMFC chair says global economy resilient; delegates walk out on Russian official
items.blurb: The IMF's steering committee named rapid AI development as a global risk, warning poorer countries are left out of AI's value chain.

items.title: A scoping review of bias in large AI models for medicine and healthcare
items.blurb: Bias in medical AI models spans many clinical settings, and the field still lacks shared fairness definitions and benchmarks.

items.title: AI tokenmaxxing at work: Paysend CEO limits AI access to top employees
items.blurb: One CEO rations general AI tools to proven performers, while UK research finds productivity gains rarely show up as revenue.

items.title: AI rapidly improving, could vastly boost U.S. GDP, Anthropic's Clark tells policymakers
items.blurb: Anthropic's Jack Clark urged world finance officials to set serious AI rules soon, citing an internal forecast of large US output gains.
